channel.title: ada-media
channel.description: Daily build notes from an open-source project in progress.

item.title: The case of the phantom panels
item.description: An empty note and a media window appeared without being asked, and neither could be dismissed. Today's fix: panels that only exist when requested — and the start of note deletion.
item.content:encoded:
In code

Commits below are in project-ada-xr.

  • Not committed — no commit landed in project-ada-xr on this date; the panel fix went out front-end-only, and the changes below are from the session.
  • Idle media surface removed — the media state reported closed while a standalone media control stayed visible in XR. The idle surface is gone; the grid, titles and input targets now stay hidden until an explicit open/show/play request. Close, tracking/focus loss and finished exports can't reopen it.
  • Note deletion (in progress) — spatial notes had no delete control. Adding a delete action and a way to hide the note panel that's showing it.

In the headset

  • The phantom note — an empty "Untitled Note" appeared without being asked: "That's strange... Can you remove it? I don't want it." Ada found it but had no delete control.
    Evidence: com.oculus.browser-20261021-135013-0.mp4 @ 0:10–1:50.
  • The media window that wouldn't leave — "It shouldn't just stay up here. It should only open when I ask for something." The state said closed; the standalone control was still visible.
    Evidence: com.oculus.browser-20261021-135013-0.mp4 @ 0:51–3:02.
  • Always paired? — "I don't remember if I paired... Is there a way to always have it paired?" Screen mirroring should remember, not rely on me.
    Evidence: com.oculus.browser-20261021-135013-0.mp4 @ 4:02–4:42.
  • Front-end-only deploy — removed in code, first checks pass, testing close/hidden input/recovery; no service restart and no forced headset refresh.
    Evidence: com.oculus.browser-20261021-135013-0.mp4 @ 5:32–5:41.

Why / what I learned

  • Panels that appear without being asked are worse than missing features — they make the space feel haunted. "Only when requested" is the rule for every surface.
  • Small fixes still count as days: the goal is that every session leaves the room a little more predictable.
  • A front-end deploy is not a checkpoint. If the change isn't committed, the next session can't review it, diff it, or roll it back.

Next

  • Commit the panel fix.
  • Finish note deletion and the hide-panel behavior.
  • Make screen mirroring remember its pairing.

item.title: Ada drives Chrome from inside the headset
item.description: From VR, Ada switches Chrome tabs on the Mac, fills our YC draft and helps write the answers — while wireless ADB reconnects itself and failures stop going silent.
item.content:encoded:
In code

Commits below are in project-ada-xr.

  • Voice relocation rule — ARCHITECTURE.md now requires every AdaXR item to be relocatable by voice, not just Ada. Named-screen relocation is explicitly logged as an implementation gap. 33edc84
  • Vision + wireless startup — opaque native-XR-session token, one bounded reconnect per startup with a twelve-second budget, fresh serial/identity check before green, vision-off persistence through focus recovery, and dedupe of concurrent attempts. 636adc5 (1,573 tests, 21 assets)

The vision/startup pair was staged at 07:01; the ADB reconnect was confirmed live that evening. The browser-control and spatial-note demos exercised code already in the repo, and no other app commit landed that day.

In the headset

  • ADB reconnects itself — a new XR session brings wireless ADB up green without a screenshot: "started up connected right away... mark that done." The prompt-return fix also passed automated checks, but real headset confirmation is still pending.
    Evidence: com.oculus.vrshell-20261019-202643-0.mp4 @ 1:17–1:39 and @ 5:55–6:08.
  • Named movement works — "move Ada to the whiteboard" → "Moved beside the whiteboard." "Yep, it worked."
    Evidence: com.oculus.vrshell-20261019-202643-0.mp4 @ 1:59–3:09.
  • Pointing move fails honestly — the exact spot came through this time, but the move returned an execution failure. Ada says so, doesn't retry, and starts an investigation instead of going silent.
    Evidence: com.oculus.vrshell-20261019-202643-0.mp4 @ 3:12–5:49.
  • Chrome, controlled from VR — Ada switches to the YC application tab, maximizes it, enters "Gamology Space" and a 42-character description, saves, and verifies after reload. The form is not submitted: "Yay! Cool, thanks. It worked."
    Evidence: com.oculus.vrshell-20261019-202643-0.mp4 @ 8:05–16:22.
  • A spatial working note for the application — creates "YC Working Discussion"; asks follow-up questions, captures decisions, keeps brainstorming separate from approved wording, saves on request, fills the form only after approval, and never submits.
    Evidence: com.oculus.vrshell-20261019-202643-0.mp4 @ 17:44–18:57.
  • First-pass answer, drafted from the build — "Gamology Space is building a context-aware interface for working with AI... AdaXR brings an AI collaborator into a mixed reality workspace, where people can talk through a problem, point to relevant objects, and develop ideas using spatial notes, physical whiteboards, and their existing software."
    Evidence: com.oculus.vrshell-20261019-202643-0.mp4 @ 20:22–21:10.
  • The note only looked like one line — a screenshot review caught the working note rendering as a truncated single-line preview. The text was intact; the panel needed wrapped, multi-line, scrolling text.
    Evidence: com.oculus.vrshell-20261019-202643-0.mp4 @ 22:54–23:15.

Why / what I learned

  • The assistant stops being a chat window when it can operate the same tools I use. Chrome on the Mac is the first demo: point at the work, talk about it, let Ada do the typing.
  • The YC form is a good forcing function. A real task with real stakes exposes everything the demo hides — notes that don't render, replies that don't arrive, cubes that won't close.
  • "Every item should be relocatable by just a voice command" is now a product rule, not a one-off request. The mirrored screen can't do it yet, and that's an implementation gap worth naming.
    Evidence: com.oculus.browser-20261019-063325-0.mp4 @ 3:49–4:17.
  • Watching Ada work in Chrome while I sat in the headset was the first time the assistant felt like it was inside my actual software instead of a demo panel beside it.

Next

  • Finish the wrapped, scrollable note rendering and the worker-cube lifecycle repair.
  • Fix the pointing-move execution failure without replaying the failed request.
  • Keep pushing the remote-control flow; make screen pairing survive a restart.

item.title: Ada gets eyes
item.description: Screenshots from the headset land in a movable photo panel, the main window shows vision + ADB + room status at a glance, and Mac screen sharing gets a standalone, billboarded view.
item.content:encoded:
In code

Commits below are in project-ada-xr.

  • Full-view vision — fresh Quest system-composite capture including passthrough and virtual content, request-bound capture leases, strict JPEG handling and same-image authenticated display. 14ea0fd (1,452 tests at the first release)
  • Photo panel — independent head-facing image, native one-hand move, proportional two-hand resize, compact red Close and near/far interaction; vision settings grouped and normally hidden. 14ea0fd (1,457 → 1,491 tests)
  • Permission + readiness — separate Vision permission, actual wireless ADB state, loaded room data, restored contents and current tracking. Stale results expire; configuration alone can't claim a connection. 14ea0fd (1,518 tests)
  • Room continuity, queue and worker tail — one safe saved-room restore per new XR session, aimed queue scrolling, stopped ducklings keeping their released trail, and transient-only notifications. 14ea0fd
  • Mac screen sharing — view-only desktop publisher/broker/viewer, then a photo-like standalone frame with near/far move, resize, red × and independent billboarding. Frontend-only activation at 21:32. The legacy tab extension and remote pointer/wheel/key/text path were retired. 14ea0fd bd3cbf1 (1,540 → 1,537 tests, 23 rendered checks)
  • Honest action failures — prepared a move once instead of twice, and separated failure communication from action-success verification so a blocked action still explains itself. 1,547 repair checks, staged at the end of the day. 14ea0fd

In the headset

  • Ada gets eyes — a fresh capture of the real room: "A dark Dell monitor, rows of drive bays, equipment with green indicator lights, black cases on the left, and cables on the right." The same image opened in the photo panel.
    Evidence: com.oculus.vrshell-20261018-142446-0.mp4 @ 5:38–6:53.
  • Vision on isn't a connection — the setting said on while the headset capture link was disconnected. The new main window separates vision permission from wireless ADB, checks every few seconds, and lets stale status expire.
    Evidence: com.oculus.vrshell-20261018-164106-0.mp4 @ 3:55–4:50 and @ 6:15–7:49; com.oculus.vrshell-20261018-173757-0.mp4 @ 0:15–1:35.
  • Status lights accepted — vision permission on, wireless ADB connected: "It worked!" and a screenshot of the real desk plus the virtual menu.
    Evidence: com.oculus.vrshell-20261018-173757-0.mp4 @ 1:00–1:35.
  • The photo panel — "I like the update... zooming works... closing works." Asked for distance grab, automatic safe room restore, and removal of the unused notification.
    Evidence: com.oculus.vrshell-20261018-173757-0.mp4 @ 1:56–2:27, @ 3:52–4:48 and @ 7:24–8:25.
  • Movement bugs classified — released ducklings snap into a line; a change in the other hand cancels a valid drag; the queue won't scroll past three; Combine stops working past three queued cues.
    Evidence: com.oculus.vrshell-20261018-132641-0.mp4 @ 3:52–4:17 and @ 8:06–8:56.
  • The silent failure — "move to second desk" failed, and the explanation appeared on the Mac but not in XR dialogue. Cause: the action-verification gate swallowed the entire final reply. Repair staged with 1,547 tests.
    Evidence: com.oculus.vrshell-20261018-203639-0.mp4 @ 1:52–4:43 and @ 17:07–17:21.
  • Screen sharing starts — pairing code, Mac page, Chrome "Entire Screen." The stream wasn't live yet; the screen became a standalone billboarded view with its own stop control.
    Evidence: com.oculus.vrshell-20261018-203639-0.mp4 @ 10:06–10:34 and @ 18:37–19:10.

Why / what I learned

  • "Can you see this?" becomes a real question once screenshots work. The status lights mean I don't have to guess whether the headset is connected before asking for something.
  • A status light has to measure the thing it names. "Vision on" was permission, not a capture connection — showing them as separate lines fixed the lie.
  • Most of the day was the unglamorous middle: capture mismatches, snapback paths, stale status, a swallowed failure message. Failure paths deserve the same care as features, especially when the assistant is supposed to be trustworthy.

Next

  • Distance grab for the photo and developer panels.
  • Exact palm targeting, drag-release retention and finished-cube cleanup.
  • Combine with the grid on; the first live screen-stream test.

item.title: Keep listening, and Ada learns to move
item.description: Hold an index finger up and pauses stop cutting my speech off; by evening Ada glides to the whiteboard on command with her ducklings trailing — and the daily log gets a repo that turns one note into posts for six platforms.
item.content:encoded:
In code

Commits below are in project-ada-xr. Today ARCHITECTURE.md also became the single product contract, with deploy-after-change as the default. 0552a5a d095640

  • Visible message queue — a pending column beside chat with per-item Remove and exact Stop targeting. Stale controls can't abort newly running work; reconnect requires a fresh snapshot and never resends. 61af65f (1,014 tests)
  • Natural deletion — request-bound intent replaces the exact-phrase gate while keeping original target/generation, one-use authority, receipts and ACKs. 17ec165 (994 tests)
  • Keep listening + presence — raised-index capture hold with scoped renewable leases; dialogue-relative home, gentle edge glide and bounded gutters for up to six worker/label pairs. acd53b4 (1,054 tests)
  • Movement — deliberate relocation by drag or named surface, exact palm-point custody, animated glide, named-destination precedence and curved worker trailing. Combine, finished-task close and follow landed in the same checkpoint. acd53b4 (1,114 → 1,260 tests)
  • Worker lifecycle + schema repair — coalesced progress no longer invalidates lifecycle authority; provider-normalized capability descriptors survive; live review-and-close verified. acd53b4 (1,171 → 1,349 tests, 108 published schema cases)
  • Shared experience context — one immutable bounded input record for selection/status, speech timing, public conversation and playback reports, with detached evidence reads and lifecycle/projection repairs. e2146e2 3ba2e4c (942 → 961 tests)
  • This log shipped — the ada-media repo turns one daily note into the site plus copy-paste posts for X, Threads, Instagram, Facebook, TikTok and YouTube. Manual posting only, no API keys. aae6fd3 62e96d8 2d8d435 153275d (ada-media)

In the headset

  • Speech matches chat — "your speech is now matching what I see on the main chat... good job."
    Evidence: 2026-10-17 09-44-40.mov @ 2:09–2:23.
  • The magic phrase bug, reproduced — "I have to say the exact same phrase to get it triggered, which is not the expected outcome."
    Evidence: 2026-10-17 09-44-40.mov @ 5:15–5:24.
  • Keep listening accepted — held a raised index through a pause: "I am holding my finger for a few seconds and it's still listening... This is a much needed feature so I don't get cut off."
    Evidence: com.oculus.vrshell-20261017-121237-0.mp4 @ 2:53–3:34.
  • Named instruction beats selection — with the grid on, the selected surface shouldn't win: "follow my verbal instruction rather than whatever is selected." Normal use should be the space's label, not diagnostic geometry.
    Evidence: com.oculus.browser-20261017-173947-0.mp4 @ 5:56–6:46.
  • Relocation, palm target, ducklings — "move to the server rack" → smooth glide with the children following; palm targeting "worked beautifully." The move's internal confirmation still failed.
    Evidence: com.oculus.vrshell-20261017-190245-0.mp4 @ 2:08–3:29.
  • Combine + worker close — "I can confirm the combined speech queue works... mark that complete." One finished cube disappeared; others stayed stuck.
    Evidence: com.oculus.vrshell-20261017-190245-0.mp4 @ 5:29–8:11.

Why / what I learned

  • "A pause shouldn't mean you've finished thinking." That's the right bar for the interaction: hold my intent, don't make me hold its rules.
  • Ada's movement is basic right now, but it's headed somewhere deliberate: leave her on the desk, have her follow me around, or tell her a place and she hovers there. Position and animation are the visual cue that makes her feel present — the foundation for the embodiment work ahead.
    Evidence: com.oculus.browser-20261017-125302-0.mp4 @ 5:25–7:01.
  • The loop is becoming the product: issue in the headset → sub-agent builds the fix → release deploys → headset confirms it, all in one day. By closeout that was 1,349 tests and a live review-and-close.
  • The log itself is part of the build now. One note becomes the site and six platform drafts, but I still post by hand — the automation stops at the clipboard.

Next

  • Movement cleanup: combine with grid on, named movement with grid hidden, drag-release position, palm-target confirmation.
  • Finished worker cubes that actually close.
  • Keep-listening cleanup: release grace, mute and tracking loss.

item.title: The room becomes editable
item.description: Naming, relabeling and deleting the room around me — 8 surfaces deleted, 5 labels kept, saved as workspace revision 5 — plus worker cubes and speech that finally matches chat.
item.content:encoded:
In code

Commits below are in project-ada-xr.

  • Worker cubes — scoped OpenClaw background tasks projected as task-linked cubes beside Ada. State comes from real observations, not animation or model wording, and conversation stays available while workers run. 05853fc
  • Worker lifecycle + audio ownership — single-owner speech, separate Stop speaking / Stop current execution, isolated worker audio and a repaired lifecycle reconciliation. 71b627f
  • Palm selection, labels and menus — semantic surface selection with stable ID and generation, passive name tags that hide on tracking loss, typed receipt-backed menu navigation, and the existing saved-content Restore path. 09ea76e
  • Safe surface deletion — typed surface.delete with original-target/generation custody, same-turn query/apply, receipts and ACKs. It edits AdaXR's workspace copy, never Quest's room scan. 09ea76e
  • Speech now equals chat — removed generated status voice, timers and separate spoken summaries. Public assistant text feeds dialogue and TTS once, in order, and an unproven final is withheld from both. 09ea76e
  • Release — final 930/930 tests, 8/8 panels, 19 assets. Workspace revision 5 held 50 surfaces, 5 retained renames and 8 deleted surfaces with no unsaved changes. 09ea76e

In the headset

  • Naming the room — select, tag, rename: main desk, main screen, whiteboard, walls, server rack.
    Evidence: 2026-10-16 15-51-15.mov @ 8:35–17:00.
  • Worker cubes appear — sub-agent spawning with little cubes worked. Closing them did not.
    Evidence: 2026-10-16 15-51-15.mov @ 15:35–18:48.
  • The room reads like an interface — grid, blue outlines, labels and the restored room all on at once: "This is great... The blue outlines and labels are working."
    Evidence: com.oculus.vrshell-20261016-183455-0.mp4 @ 0:00–1:29.
  • Speech fixed — "the chat has been fixed. That's great." Then: stream updates as they arrive instead of one giant block at the end.
    Evidence: com.oculus.vrshell-20261016-201025-0.mp4 @ 1:23 and @ 4:12–4:42.
  • Delete works; the magic phrase doesn't — deletion landed, but only when I used the exact wording: "You shouldn't need a magic phrase."
    Evidence: com.oculus.vrshell-20261016-203321-0.mp4 @ 2:50–7:52.
  • Revision 5 saved — "Workspace Revision 5 is saved with 50 surfaces and no unsaved changes... all five renamed labels are retained and all eight deleted surfaces are absent."
    Evidence: com.oculus.vrshell-20261016-203321-0.mp4 @ 19:50–19:57.
  • Nine-minute silence + queue request — "we've waited for nine minutes and it's not doing anything." The queue needs to be visible, changeable and removable.
    Evidence: 2026-10-16 18-11-48.mov @ 11:18–11:48 (nine-minute quote); 2026-10-16 17-17-56.mov @ 22:14–22:49 (queue request).

Why / what I learned

  • The room stops being a picture the moment you can edit it. Renaming a table is small; realizing you can delete it and rebuild the space is the door opening.
  • The bug of the day came from being too literal — deletion demanded an exact phrase. Intent, not incantations.
  • Delegation is not completion. The worker cubes made that visible: a task can be done without being reviewed, closed, or actually finished from my side.
  • Speech should be the chat, not a performance around it. One text, two surfaces, in order.

Next

  • A visible, removable message queue.
  • Sub-agents that close themselves when they finish.
  • Natural deletion wording.
  • No more nine-minute stalls with zero feedback.

item.title: Ada grows hands
item.description: Every WebXR hand overlay on at once — joint markers, radius spheres, aim rays, orientation lines — plus a cyan index-finger ray, the first developer preset, and the browser panel's first build.
item.content:encoded:
In code

Commits below are in project-ada-xr.

  • Hand visualization — generated controls for joint markers, joint radii, orientation axes and browser aim rays, plus a cyan index-finger ray derived from tip-minus-distal joints. Tracking loss hides invalid geometry. fd1be1c
  • Browser panel — Chrome helper and same-tab video/audio sharing with pointer, scroll, drag and text input. Consent, input ownership and revocation are explicit; hiding the panel revokes sharing, mutes its audio and clears held input. fd1be1c
  • Capability library — typed, receipt-backed discovery and controls for room visibility, semantic surface inspection, highlighting, names and categories. fd1be1c
  • Developer settings — room/workspace, capabilities and browser controls hidden under one developer area, one subsection at a time, with room and hand state preserved across menu changes. fd1be1c
  • Meaningful capture — the meaningful-v1 policy keeps useful interaction evidence instead of noisy repeated observations; 18,755 old rows were cleared while the saved room, notes and canonical chat were preserved. fd1be1c
  • Resilient queued voice — bounded backend FIFO, exact Stop, capture-time target pinning, commit-before-playback and a separate audio FIFO. Final release: 541 tests, 8/8 panels, 19 assets. fd1be1c

In the headset

  • Every overlay at once — joint markers, radii, orientation lines and aim rays on both hands, then the cyan index-finger ray: "Perfect. This is working perfectly."
    Evidence: 2026-10-15 17-19-59.mov @ 1:21–2:07.
  • First developer preset — saved the all-white hand view (markers, radii, Z orientation, aim rays) to project memory. Selectable presets are still missing: "we have to do better than project memory."
    Evidence: com.oculus.browser-20261015-154745-0.mp4 @ 7:40–9:05.
  • Three mystery panels — identified the room panel, capability catalog and browser-sharing panel: "It lets you view and control a Mac Chrome tab inside XR." Asked to collapse them into Developer settings.
    Evidence: com.oculus.vrshell-20261015-172022-0.mp4 @ 3:14–4:51.
  • Speech bug logged — Ada answered a sentence I never said: "I didn't say any of that. Let's book that as a bug."
    Evidence: com.oculus.browser-20261015-154745-0.mp4 @ 6:12–6:27.
  • Headset-off stall — the build wasn't dead; it stopped when the headset came off: "I think it stopped building when I took the headset off."
    Evidence: com.oculus.browser-20261015-164602-0.mp4 @ 5:21–5:57.
  • Browser test started, not finished — Mac Chrome tab in Quest, video/audio first, then input. The session ended with "something is interrupting it," so this one stays open.
    Evidence: 2026-10-15 20-25-30.mov @ 0:36–10:29.

Why / what I learned

  • Hands are how a room becomes an interface. If I can point at a surface and have Ada know exactly what I mean, the whole space becomes addressable.
  • Watching the raw tracking data while building against it is the whole trick: you can't debug an interaction you can't see.
  • The headset-off stall is why work has to survive the headset leaving the head. Queued voice and single-owner audio came out of that.
  • Presets belong in the app, not in project memory — a dev view I can't recall isn't really a preset.

Next

  • Finish the browser roundtrip: real Chrome → Quest video, audio, then clicking, scrolling and typing.
  • Move hand presets out of project memory and into the app.
  • Chase the wrong-text speech bug.

item.title: Ada, take four
item.description: The fourth attempt at Ada starts here: the room imports, anchors and saves as a workspace — and the whole attempt gets logged in the open, one day at a time.
item.content:encoded:
In code

Commits below are in project-ada-xr.

  • Room workspace v1 — Quest room import, a five-step guided setup (align → import → check → anchor → save), up to 64 named surfaces and 50 notes in one spatial root, a persistent anchor and aligned restore. Saving is explicit; nothing autosaves. f57d060
  • Spatial notes — create/read/append and desktop export, with sanitized Markdown filenames, private-state path checks and symlink guards. 6bd79fe
  • Voice hardening — note-save authorization, TTS audio validation and gateway recovery-race tests; local voice workflows became recoverable instead of silently dropping work. 6bd79fe
  • Fresh-only capture — capture policy v1: historical replay omitted, payloads capped at 48 KB, secrets redacted, private outbox enforced. Capture is observation evidence, not conversation memory. 1dd1cef
  • Agent rules — AGENTS.md updated with the development contract for the attempt. ea400e6

In the headset

No video from this day — I didn't record the first session. The first recorded session is tomorrow.

  • Workspace walkthrough — aligned room import, persistent anchor, local save, and restore after an XR re-entry and full page reload — confirmed at 20:01 PDT.

Why / what I learned

  • I'm officially starting the fourth attempt at Ada today. This is its first entry.
  • The frame for this attempt: Ada lives in the room. It's in the headset with me, in my actual scanned space — the grid, the outlines, every surface it can find and name. Voice in, voice out, and it runs its own little sub-agents while we work.
  • A workspace that survives a reload is the difference between a demo and a place to work. The first session was mostly plumbing — import, anchors, save, restore — and that plumbing is what lets every later session start in the same room instead of from scratch.
  • Attempt four gets a trail. If this one works, the day-by-day of how it got there — including everything that didn't work — is the interesting part.
  • Open development from the start: these notes go up as they're written, not once they're pretty.

Next

  • First recorded build session: bring the room up, then start with what Ada can find, see and name in it.
